hook: Corinna Cortes earned a masters degree in physics from the University of Copenhagen before completing a PhD in computer science at the University of Rochester in 1993. She joined AT&T Bell Labs in 1989, where she spent more than a decade in the Adaptive Systems Research Group led by Larry Jackel. There she and Vladimir Vapnik developed the soft margin support vector machine, an extension that made support vector machines practical for real world classification problems with noisy, non separable data. Their 1995 paper on support vector networks became one of the most cited papers in machine learning. She later moved to Google, where she founded and now leads Google Research New York as a Vice President, overseeing large scale machine learning research across multiple international teams.

standing.standing: Corinna Cortes is Vice President of Google Research, where she founded and now leads the New York lab and oversees large scale machine learning research across multiple international teams. Her standing in the field rests chiefly on the soft margin support vector machine, which she and Vladimir Vapnik developed at AT&T Bell Labs and described in their 1995 paper on support vector networks, one of the most cited papers in machine learning. That extension made support vector machines practical for real world classification problems involving noisy, non separable data. She holds a masters degree in physics from the University of Copenhagen and a PhD in computer science from the University of Rochester, completed in 1993, and spent more than a decade in the Adaptive Systems Research Group led by Larry Jackel. Her recorded recognition includes the AT&T Science and Technology Medal in 2000 for work on data mining in very large data sets and a shared ACM Paris Kanellakis Theory and Practice Award with Vapnik in 2008. Google is the only company on this site where she is recorded as an executive.
